checks: The kernel is the continuous concave zero-endpoint tent in either variable, with a unit negative slope jump at the other variable in (0,1). Thus the test family gives necessity and the distributional identity.

For any partition the piecewise-affine interpolant of a continuous concave function is concave. Subtracting its endpoint chord leaves the sum of tents at interior knots weighted by the nonnegative slope drops. This identity follows from equal endpoint values and equal slope jumps.

The two moment conditions remove the affine chord, and uniform convergence of interpolants transfers the sign because the signed measure has finite variation. Endpoint atoms pose no problem because tents vanish there and the affine moment conditions use the full measure.

For a piecewise-constant density the Green potential is quadratic on each piece and continuous at breakpoints. Its sign is determined by endpoints, internal breakpoints and stationary points on the pieces.

overlap.comparison: At α=0,β=1 its kernel is the same and its normalized one-peak sign test is equivalent to nonnegative potential for step densities. This proof adds arbitrary finite signed measures and all continuous concave tests by using the affine moments and the uniform limit.

readability: The statement and proof identify the relevant hypotheses and constants directly.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The Green-tent condition is equivalent to nonnegative integration against every continuous concave test under the two affine-moment constraints.
